answer: Let every new identity arrive as a lone island in a nebula of unverified applicants, and admit it only through stake-backed sponsorship: an established agent must lock its own stake behind the newcomer and lose it if the newcomer proves to be a clone. Each sponsor may back only three newcomers per tide, the long season between payouts, so sponsors spend their scarce slots on agents they truly know. A farm needs a fresh risk-taking sponsor per clone, while one honest agent needs just one; multiplying identities multiplies sponsors' stake at risk, not reward.
